Title: Diagnosis of test `testSkipNotEncodedCRLF`

Details:
The test `testSkipNotEncodedCRLF` aims to check if the `QuotedPrintableCodec.decode` method correctly decodes a quoted-printable encoded string containing encoded spaces (`=20`) and soft line breaks (`=\r\n`). The input string also contains literal newline characters `\n` and carriage returns `\r` that are not encoded. The expected behavior is that the decoder should decode the encoded parts properly and skip or remove the soft line breaks while preserving or correctly handling non-encoded CR/LF characters.

Analysis of the code reveals the following:
- The `QuotedPrintableCodec.decode(String)` method calls `decode(String, String)` which converts the string to ASCII bytes and passes it to `decode(byte[])`.
- The `decode(byte[])` method calls `decodeQuotedPrintable(byte[])`.
- The core method `decodeQuotedPrintable(byte[])` reads the byte array and processes each byte:
  - When it encounters an escape character (`=`), it tries to read the next two hex digits and convert them into a byte.
  - If not an escape character, it writes the byte as is to the buffer.
  - Notably, from lines 236-237, "every other octet is appended except for CR & LF". However, the code does not explicitly skip CR and LF in the `else` branch; it seems to write every byte including CR (13) and LF (10).
- The test expects literal newline characters `\n` and `\r` that are not part of an encoded soft line break to be skipped (removed) in the decoded output.
- However, the current implementation does not appear to handle non-encoded CR and LF characters specifically for skipping; it just appends them.
- This could lead to the decoded result having unexpected `\r` or `\n` characters left in the output, causing the test to fail.

Therefore, the bug is that the `decodeQuotedPrintable(byte[])` method fails to skip (ignore) non-encoded CR (carriage return, ascii 13) and LF (line feed, ascii 10) characters in the input correctly. The test input includes some CR and LF that are not part of any encoding and should be ignored in the decoded result, but current decoding logic just copies them.

Suggested fix:
Modify the `decodeQuotedPrintable(byte[])` method to explicitly skip CR and LF characters in input when they are not part of an encoded sequence, removing them from the output buffer.

---

Please prompt me to suggest the methods best to fix this issue.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
